tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description specifies exactly when to use the skill (model call failures, 5xx, throttling, latency degradation, empty responses, status questions) and explicitly carves out exclusions ('Do not load it for a symptom that names no model call'). It focuses on the triage scenario (user intent: determine who's at fault) rather than internal mechanics, and while long, it is a single dense paragraph covering many trigger phrasings deliberately per best practice of being pushy with explicit contexts.
tests.evidence: "Triage a live failure where a model call is in the failing path ... Use it when model invocations error or return 5xx, are throttled (429s), time out, get slower or have degraded TimeToFirstToken, return empty, fail only after a deploy..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific overall (good), but it is extremely verbose and repetitive in places — e.g. the 'Before You Present' checklist re-states the same rules (no pending work, three blocks, UNDETERMINED entrances) that are already stated earlier in 'The rules every answer keeps', and several paragraphs restate the same point (e.g. conclusion must have a next step) in multiple sections. This bloats every activation's context.
tests.evidence: **Never end your turn while work you started is still running.** ... An answer that says "I'm now searching the logs and will pull it together once both come back" is not an answer
tests.recommendation: Consolidate the repeated rules (pending-work warning, three-block contract, UNDETERMINED gate) into a single canonical location and have other sections reference it rather than restating it in full.
